source: Watermelon (ដំណាំ ឪឡឹក) cultivation factsheet, undated; source publisher not stated on the visible pages but the structure and layout are consistent with MAFF/GDA vegetable-crop factsheet series (elibrary.maff.gov.kh). Uploaded PDF, no cover page present.
text:
Watermelon has traditionally been grown along riverbanks and lake margins, and in areas that were formerly rice fields before the war, particularly in border zones such as Kampong Thom and Kampong Cham/Kratie areas along the Mekong and lowland zones.

Seed selection criteria include knowing the source, production month and year, purity, and germination rate; only seed recommended for use should be selected.

For land and soil selection, farmers should choose sandy loam, sandy, reddish soil from foothills, or well-drained clay-loam soils with good structure that allow water to drain quickly, with a soil pH of about 5 to 6.8, which is considered medium. Soil that is too acidic, such as areas previously used for jute, tobacco, or watermelon in earlier seasons, or heavy clay soil (referred to as 'Glay Soil'), should be avoided.

For land preparation, farmers should first clear all weeds and crop residues from the previous planting, then plow the land and let it sit for a period to allow the sun to kill soil-borne pests and other residues, after which the soil is broken up and leveled. Plowing and harrowing should be done 2-3 times to make the soil friable, followed by application of compound fertilizer (formulation 15-15-15) at a rate of about 200 kg per hectare spread on the soil surface, then covering or ridging so that the field is ready for sowing.

Watermelon can be grown in most regions from October to December and January to February; in higher, drier land areas it can also be grown from around July/August through October. Germination is favored by temperatures around 15-22°C at emergence, with flowering favored around 24°C, and general growth favored by daytime temperatures of about 25-30°C and nighttime temperatures of about 20-24°C. Most varieties need adequate moisture during the germination stage.
